newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady to weaker in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady to weaker in quiet trade.

text.p: Med oil products were steady to slightly weaker in quiet trade on Friday.
Gas oil came under pressure with local Med demand remaining muted and only limited interest from out of the region seen.
Good supplies, particularly of Russian material, along with mild temperatures were the main causes of the lacklustre demand.
Russian talked at high cif quotes -75 cents cif Genoa for Feb material while FOD was pegged around high fob quotes flat.
High sulphur fuel oil was little changed although isolated requirements for different qualities were still outstanding, traders said.
Low sulphur cargoes were around $1 firmer although recent trades to players seeking to cover existing commitments seem to have taken some of the obvious prompt length out of the market.
Cargo offers were pegged at around $111 cif Italy. But end user buying in Italy remains slack.

Gasoline was steady to slightly with most attention focused on northwest Europe which has weakened over the past few days due to the closure of arbitrage to United States and generally lower crude prices.

Brokers said that Mediterranean prices would ease much further because there were no unsold cargoes left for the rest of February and there was healthy demand for low and medium octane material from the Lebanon, Africa and South America.
Naphtha was unchanged at a notional $221/$223 cif, in line with northwest Europe which held relatively firm in Friday's session.
